text: Why is it so easy to fix a friend's problem, but so hard to fix yours?
say: Why is it so easy to fix a friend's problem, but so hard to fix yours?

text: It's called Solomon's paradox. A king wise for everyone, except himself.
say: It's called Solomon's paradox. A king, wise for everyone, except himself.

text: Your friend gets a rude text? You say, let it go. You get one? You replay it all night.
say: Your friend gets a rude text? You say, let it go. You get one? You replay it all night.

text: Distance makes us wise. Up close, feelings fog the view.
say: Distance makes us wise. Up close, feelings fog the view.

text: So step back and ask, what would I tell a friend? And check on the friend who always gives advice.
say: So step back, and ask, what would I tell a friend? And check on the friend who always gives advice.
